subject: english
question:
Choose the correct meaning of idiom:

**Move heaven and earth**

options.text: To work tirelessly to achieve something

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. To work tirelessly to achieve something .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Move heaven and earth"** signifies making immense efforts or going to great lengths to achieve a goal.
 
• This phrase is often used to describe determination and tireless effort in pursuit of something important.
 
• It does not imply relocating, staying silent, or following blindly.

Correct sentence: *If someone says they will move heaven and earth to help, they mean they will put in extraordinary effort to ensure success.*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Idioms enrich language by expressing meanings that are often figurative, rather than literal.
 
• Understanding idioms helps in interpreting the deeper, culturally relevant meaning of expressions.
